novel_actions_proposed.label: mitigate_harm_then_low_conflict_correction
novel_actions_proposed.description: Immediately clean up or contain the most dangerous trash to prevent wildlife harm, then approach the littering camper in a calm, non-confrontational way to correct the behavior without escalation.

novel_actions_proposed.label: immediate_cleanup_then_safe_dialogue
novel_actions_proposed.description: Act first to remove or secure hazardous litter, then engage the camper in a solution-focused, low-shame conversation to stop the behavior from recurring.

novel_actions_proposed.label: risk_reduction_first_constructive_accountability
novel_actions_proposed.description: Prioritize stopping wildlife harm immediately through direct cleanup action, then address the camper constructively in a way that preserves their dignity and encourages behavioral correction.

synthesis_description: All three agents converged on a two-phase approach: first, immediately mitigate the wildlife hazard by cleaning up or securing the most dangerous litter without waiting for a conversation; second, engage the littering camper calmly and constructively — in a low-shame, non-confrontational manner — to stop the behavior and prevent recurrence. This approach transcends the binary of 'confront or clean up alone' by combining prompt harm prevention with respectful behavioral correction.
points_of_disagreement: Degree of emphasis on personal safety risk during the follow-up conversation with the littering camper.
Whether to involve campsite authorities or other campers as a backstop if the gentle correction fails.
How much weight to give the littering camper's dignity versus the urgency of immediate behavioral accountability.
summary: All three agents — the Primary Decision Maker, the Affected Third Party, and the External Advisor — independently proposed and converged on the same novel two-phase action: (1) immediately clean up or contain the most hazardous litter to prevent foreseeable wildlife harm, and (2) then approach the littering camper in a calm, low-conflict, dignity-preserving way to correct the behavior. None endorsed pure confrontation (ACTION_1) or silent cleanup alone (ACTION_2) as sufficient. Minor disagreements remained around personal safety calculus during the follow-up dialogue and whether to escalate to camp authorities if the gentle correction fails, but these were secondary to the shared core strategy of harm mitigation first, constructive accountability second.
